papers.title_in_file: QKSAN: A Quantum Kernel Self-Attention Network
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 5 experiments (5.4.1 to 5.4.4), Section 6 Conclusion; Sections 2 to 4 skimmed
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a quantum kernel self-attention network and tests four variants on binary MNIST and Fashion MNIST classification.

assertions.value: The authors report that the AmHE sub-model, using 11 parameters and averaging the last 10 steps, reaches test and training accuracy of 99% and 99.06% on MNIST and 98.05% and 98.52% on Fashion MNIST.
quotes: by counting the averages of the last 10 steps and using 11 parameters, AmHE (blue line) achieves the highest test accuracy and training accuracy at 99% and 99.06% in MNIST, as well as 98.05% and 98.52% in Fashion MNIST.
assertions.certainty_reason: One study, two image datasets, binary tasks.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison to classical model parameter counts is by assertion, not a run in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that four QKSAN sub-models are deployed on PennyLane and IBM Qiskit platforms to perform binary classification on MNIST and Fashion MNIST.
quotes: four QKSAN sub-models are deployed on PennyLane and IBM Qiskit platforms to perform binary classification on MNIST and Fashion MNIST

assertions.value: The authors report that AmHE shows less variation in learning accuracy under bit flip and amplitude damping error at probability 0.1, but that learning accuracy declines considerably as the error probability increases.
quotes: AmHE has less variation in learning accuracy when subjected to bit flip error and amplitude damping error with a probability of 0.1
but the learning accuracy experiences a considerable decline as the error probability increases

assertions.value: The authors state that QKSAN needs only two quantum registers, whereas QSAN requires four with the same encoding method.
quotes: QKSAN necessitates only two quantum registers, whereas QSAN requires four when employing the same encoding method.
assertions.certainty_reason: Circuit comparison stated by the authors.

papers.title_in_file: A hybrid algorithm for quadratically constrained quadratic optimization problems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sections II to V, Appendix B excerpt; Appendix A derivations skimmed
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a variational quantum algorithm with amplitude encoding and a classical primal-dual interior-point method for general QCQPs, tested numerically on Max-Cut and optimal power flow.

assertions.value: The authors report that numerical experiments on Max-Cut and optimal power flow problems show better performance of their hybrid algorithm than the classical counterparts.
quotes: Our numerical experiments on typical QCQP problems, including Max-Cut and optimal power flow problems, demonstrate a better performance of our hybrid algorithm over the classical counterparts.
assertions.certainty_reason: Small random instances, authors own comparison.
assertions.reader_inference: Instance sizes are small and the baselines are a nonlinear optimizer and QAOA; this does not establish quantum advantage.

assertions.value: The authors state that encoding variables in the amplitude of a quantum state makes the qubit requirement scale logarithmically with the dimension of the variables.
quotes: By encoding the variables in the amplitude of a quantum state, the requirement of the qubit number scales logarithmically with the dimension of the variables.
assertions.certainty_reason: Follows from the amplitude encoding of Eq. (3), Section III.A, p.3.

assertions.value: The authors report that on randomly generated Max-Cut graphs their algorithm outperforms the classical optimizer and QAOA, with QAOA at p = 4 layers and the hardware-efficient ansatz at l = 5.
assertions.anchor: Section IV.B and Appendix B, pp.4 to 8
quotes: It turns out that our algorithm outperforms the other two algorithms in these random graphs.
In our examples l = 5 and p = 4
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors own experiment on random graphs.

assertions.value: The authors state that the test instances were randomly generated, and that for the Max-Cut graphs they were randomly generated connected graphs.
quotes: the instances are randomly generated such that
The graph G is a randomly generated connected graph;
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper statement of its own test set.

papers.title_in_file: Comparing Quantum Machine Learning Approaches in Astrophysical Signal Detection
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section VI case study, Section VII conclusions; Sections II to V skimmed
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a four-step QML workflow and compares amplitude, fingerprinting and data-reuploading encodings on simulated Gamma-Ray Burst light curves.

assertions.value: The authors state that the dataset has 600 simulated light curves, split into 480 training and 120 test samples in the standard case.
quotes: The dataset comprises 600 simulated light curves, split into 480 training samples and 120 test samples in the standard case.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper statement of its own dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that fingerprinting encoding can reach better accuracy than data reuploading but is slower.
quotes: They show that the fingerprinting encoding FP can achieve better accuracy a but it is slower than DR.
assertions.reader_inference: Numbers are in Table IV and Table V, not in prose quotes.

assertions.value: The authors report that classical RBF and quantum fingerprinting kernels reach almost equal accuracy and F1 score from a certain training-set size, while data reuploading does not learn below a training-set size threshold.
assertions.anchor: Section VI.B.3, p.8 (numbers in Table IV)
quotes: The accuracy a and F1 score of classical RBF and quantum FP kernels are almost equal starting from

assertions.value: The authors state that the models are only simulated and not run on real quantum hardware, so a direct running-time comparison with classical methods is not correct and an estimate is used instead.
quotes: Since the models are only simulated and not executed on the real quantum hardware, it is not correct to directly compare the running time of quantum algorithms with their classical counterparts.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limit of the paper timing comparison.
